Now let me compile the most comprehensive and up-to-date scRNA-seq pipeline for you. Here is the complete blueprint: --- # 🧬 Comprehensive Standard scRNA-seq Data Analysis Pipeline ## Dual Framework: **R/Seurat (v5)** 🟢 + **Python/Scanpy** 🔵 ```mermaid graph TD Start((🎬 Start)) --> S1[Phase 1:
Read Alignment &
Quantification] S1 --> S2[Phase 2:
Quality Control
& Filtering] S2 --> S3[Phase 3:
Normalization &
HVG Selection] S3 --> S4[Phase 4:
Dimensionality
Reduction] S4 --> S5[Phase 5:
Clustering] S5 --> S6[Phase 6:
Cell Type
Annotation] S6 --> S7[Phase 7:
Downstream
Analysis] S7 --> Finish((✅ Deliverables &
Report)) subgraph Downstream[Phase 7 - Choose Your Path] D1[Differential
Expression] D2[Trajectory /
Pseudotime] D3[Cell-Cell
Communication] D4[Gene Regulatory
Networks] D5[Functional
Enrichment] end S7 --> Downstream ``` --- ## 📋 PHASE 1: Preprocessing — Alignment & Quantification | Step | Tool | Input → Output | |:-----|:-----|:---------------| | **Raw Data** | - | FASTQ files from scRNA-seq | | **Alignment** | **Cell Ranger** (10x) / **STARsolo** / **Alevin** (salmon) | FASTQ → Gene×Cell Count Matrix | | **Count Matrix** | Output format | `.mtx` (market exchange), `.h5` (HDF5), or `.tsv/.csv` | **Recommended:** Use **Cell Ranger** for 10x data, or **STARsolo** for non-10x/non-standard data. Both output a gene-barcode count matrix. --- ## 🔬 PHASE 2: Quality Control (QC) & Filtering This is the most critical step — garbage in, garbage out! ### QC Metrics to Compute: | Metric | What it Detects | Typical Threshold | |:-------|:-----------------|:------------------| | **nCount_RNA** (UMI count per cell) | Empty droplets / doublets | Remove outliers (often >500) | | **nFeature_RNA** (Genes per cell) | Empty droplets / doublets | 200-2500 (varies by cell type) | | **% Mitochondrial genes** | Dying / stressed cells | < 5-20% (5% for PBMC, up to 20% for tissues) | | **% Ribosomal genes** | Technical artifacts | Typically kept | | **Doublet detection** | Two cells in one droplet | **Scrublet** (Python) or **DoubletFinder** (R) | ### 🟢 Seurat v5 Approach ```r # Create Seurat object pbmc <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts, project = "PBMC", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200) # QC metrics pbmc[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(pbmc, pattern = "^MT-") # Filter pbmc <- subset(pbmc, subset = nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < 2500 & percent.mt < 5) ``` ### 🔵 Scanpy Approach ```python import scanpy as sc # Read data adata = sc.read_10x_mtx("data/filtered_gene_bc_matrices/hg19/") # QC metrics adata.var["mt"] = adata.var_names.str.startswith("MT-") sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics(adata, qc_vars=["mt"], percent_top=None, log1p=False) # Filter sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_genes=200) sc.pp.filter_genes(adata, min_cells=3) adata = adata[adata.obs.n_genes_by_counts < 2500, :] adata = adata[adata.obs.pct_counts_mt < 5, :] ``` --- ## ⚖️ PHASE 3: Normalization & Feature Selection ### Step 3a: Normalization | Method | Framework | Description | |:-------|:----------|:------------| | **SCTransform** 🔥 | Seurat (v5) | Regularized negative binomial — **recommended gold standard** | | **LogNormalize** | Both | Total counts → log(1+CPM) — classic, simple | | **scran** (deconvolution) | R/Bioc | Pooling-based normalization | | **Pearson residuals** | Scanpy (SCTransform equivalent) | Analytic Pearson residuals | ### 🟢 Seurat v5 (Recommended: SCTransform) ```r pbmc <- SCTransform(pbmc, vars.to.regress = "percent.mt") ``` ### 🔵 Scanpy (LogNormalize + HVG) ```python # Save raw counts adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy() # Normalize to 10,000 counts per cell and log-transform sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4) sc.pp.log1p(adata) ``` ### Step 3b: Highly Variable Gene (HVG) Selection ```r # Seurat v5 (SCTransform does this automatically) # Or manually: pbmc <- FindVariableFeatures(pbmc, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000) ``` ```python # Scanpy sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, n_top_genes=2000, batch_key="sample") adata = adata[:, adata.var.highly_variable] ``` --- ## 📉 PHASE 4: Dimensionality Reduction | Step | Method | Purpose | |:-----|:-------|:--------| | **Scaling** | `ScaleData` (R) / `sc.pp.scale` (Py) | Zero-mean, unit-variance | | **Linear DR** | **PCA** | Principal components — 30-50 PCs | | **Non-linear DR** | **UMAP** (primary) / **t-SNE** | Visualization | ### 🟢 Seurat ```r pbmc <- RunPCA(pbmc, npcs = 50, verbose = FALSE) pbmc <- RunUMAP(pbmc, dims = 1:30) ``` ### 🔵 Scanpy ```python sc.pp.scale(adata, max_value=10) sc.tl.pca(adata, n_comps=50, svd_solver="arpack") sc.pp.neighbors(adata, n_pcs=30) sc.tl.umap(adata) ``` ### **Elbow plot** — determine optimal PC count ```r ElbowPlot(pbmc, ndims = 50) ``` ```python sc.pl.pca_variance_ratio(adata, n_pcs=50, log=True) ``` --- ## 🧩 PHASE 5: Clustering ### 🟢 Seurat ```r pbmc <- FindNeighbors(pbmc, dims = 1:30) pbmc <- FindClusters(pbmc, resolution = 0.5) # Try 0.1-1.2 ``` ### 🔵 Scanpy ```python sc.tl.leiden(adata, resolution=0.5) # Leiden is the recommended algorithm ``` **Resolution Guide:** - `0.1-0.3`: Coarse clusters (major cell types) - `0.5-0.8`: Standard resolution (cell subtypes) - `1.0-1.5`: Fine-grained (rare populations) --- ## 🏷️ PHASE 6: Cell Type Annotation ### 🔹 **Option A: Manual Annotation** (Marker-based) Find cluster markers: ```r # Seurat markers <- FindAllMarkers(pbmc, only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25, logfc.threshold = 0.25) ``` ```python # Scanpy sc.tl.rank_genes_groups(adata, "leiden", method="wilcoxon") ``` **Reference Marker Databases:** | Database | URL / Source | Type | |:---------|:-------------|:-----| | **CellMarker 2.0** | http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CellMarker/ | Comprehensive | | **PanglaoDB** | https://panglaodb.se/ | scRNA-seq compendium | | **PanglaoDB (MCP)** | Available in our system | Local DB | ### 🔹 **Option B: Automatic Annotation** (Recommended for scale) | Tool | Framework | Method | |:-----|:-----------|:-------| | **SingleR** | R/Bioc | Correlation with reference | | **CellTypist** | Python | Logistic regression | | **scType** | Both | Marker-based scoring | | **Azimuth** | R/Shiny | Seurat-based reference mapping | ### 🟢 Seurat ```r library(SingleR) ref <- celldex::HumanPrimaryCellAtlasData() pred <- SingleR(test = pbmc@assays$RNA$data, ref = ref, labels = ref$label.main) pbmc$singlr_labels <- pred$pruned.labels ``` ### 🔵 Scanpy ```python # CellTypist import celltypist model = celltypist.models.Model.load(model="Immune_All_Low.pkl") predictions = celltypist.annotate(adata, model=model, majority_voting=True) ``` --- ## 🔬 PHASE 7: Downstream Analysis (Choose Your Path) ```mermaid graph LR A[Clustered & Annotated Data] --> B1[Differential
Expression] A --> B2[Trajectory /
Pseudotime] A --> B3[Cell-Cell
Communication] A --> B4[Gene Regulatory
Network] A --> B5[Functional
Enrichment] A --> B6[Multi-sample
Integration] ``` ### 7a. Differential Expression (DE) Analysis | Method | Best For | R | Python | |:-------|:---------|:--|:-------| | **Wilcoxon Rank-Sum** | Default, fast | `FindAllMarkers(assay="SCT")` | `sc.tl.rank_genes_groups()` | | **MAST** | Low dropout effects | `FindMarkers(test.use="MAST")` | `pydeseq2` | | **pseudobulk** | Biologically rigorous | `muscat` package | `pseudobulk` approach | | **DESeq2 / edgeR** | Pseudobulk counts | `DESeq2`, `edgeR` | `pydeseq2` | ### 7b. Trajectory Inference (Pseudotime) | Tool | Type | R | Python | |:-----|:-----|:--|:-------| | **Monocle 3** | Graph-based | ✅ | ❌ | | **Slingshot** | Lineage tree | ✅ | ❌ | | **Palantir** | Entropy-based | ❌ | ✅ | | **scVelo** | RNA velocity | ❌ | ✅ (recommended) | | **PAGA** | Abstract connectivity | ❌ | ✅ (part of Scanpy) | ### 7c. Cell-Cell Communication | Tool | Framework | Description | |:-----|:-----------|:------------| | **CellChat** | R 🔥 | Ligand-receptor + signaling network | | **NicheNet** | R | Ligand-target gene prediction | | **CellPhoneDB** | Python | Curated L-R interactions | | **SingleCellSignalR** | R | Simple L-R scoring | ### 7d. Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) | Tool | Framework | |:-----|:----------| | **SCENIC / pySCENIC** | Both (py recommended) | | **Pando** | R | | **CellOracle** | Python | ### 7e. 💡 Key Recommendations & Best Practices 1. **✅ ALWAYS start with SCTransform** in Seurat — it's more robust than LogNormalize 2. **✅ Check batch effects early** — PCA colored by sample can reveal integration needs 3. **✅ Use multiple annotation methods** — consensus annotation is more reliable 4. **✅ Save raw counts in a separate layer** before any normalization 5. **⚠️ Don't over-cluster** — use `clustree` (R) to assess resolution stability 6. **⚠️ Remove doublets before clustering** — doublets form their own clusters 7. **⚠️ Always check for ambient RNA** — use `SoupX` (R) or `DropletUtils` 8. **⚡ For large datasets (>100k cells)** — use `SeuratDisk` / `scvi-tools` / GPU acceleration --- ##
